authorization: Pang’s active independent PAL v2.4 construction, his direction to work from the full corpus and his question about carrying a trace forward and reading it back on the same input.

source_roles.corpus: PAL v2.4 supplies the carry and the required return. APCI motivates changing a single ordinary label on the same half-rows. RPL supplies the inherited square scales and BLA the boundary and its cost.
mathematical_inputs: The project’s original signed taper, square-pass inverse, bounded signed rectangle, and finite lower bound at a zeta zero.
Integer power sums, Möbius inversion, finite summation by parts, reciprocal interpolation, and midpoint bounds for harmonic sums.

The Gaussian localization uses the classical positive Riemann xi kernel and Jacobi theta transformation. The recurrent signs of the omitted-label measurement use the existence of a critical-line zero and a Laplace positivity argument.

formal_result: If every sufficiently late fourth-power root j has nonnegative rational first-pass value, then stock Mathlib RiemannHypothesis. The canonical finite head is independent of extra padding. The fixed reference states the hypothesis as a separate sum over ordinary Möbius marks, squared integer dilations and the physical cutoff 2*j^4. The hypothesis remains unproved.
formal_results_also_checked: Exact finite reciprocal-grid quadrature and its power-of-three output with the full and first-label-deleted receivers. Positive row weights for both and after any initial ordinary-label cutoff.
An explicit lower bound for the full one-pass cubic average at every dyadic head.
Uniform relative variation, a sufficient integer gap condition, the unaveraged seed chord and the passed fourth-power chord.
paper_results: A strongly positive interval of length at least a constant times y^(3/4)*sqrt(log y) occurs near every sufficiently large head for the same first pass. There are runs of at least a constant times sqrt(log y) positive fourth powers there.
A zero with real part beta>1/2 forces recurrent negative blocks of length at least c(rho)*y^((1+beta)/2) and at least c(rho)*j^(2*beta-1) consecutive negative fourth-root indices.

After any fixed positive fraction of the first ordinary label is removed, the normalized raw measurement has positive limsup and negative liminf. Averaging over a whole period of each square clock in the uncut reading gives a calculable straight line and a positive decaying error.

The interval sign certifications around side 432 billion use exact band counts, geometry and outward reciprocal bounds.
